paper_id: Guo et al. - 2010 - False Negative Problem of Counting Bloom Filter
title: False Negative Problem of Counting Bloom Filter
venue: IEEE Transactions on Knowledge and Data Engineering
motivation: Networking devices track flows using CBFs but don't store original data; incorrect deletions cause false negatives which wrongly reject desired objects.
problem_framing: Two types of incorrect deletion (false positive items, multiaddress items) cause false negatives in standard BF operations.
key_insight: Potential false negatives often stay unexposed; increasing bits set to value>1 without decreasing zero bits reduces exposed false negatives.
method_signature: Multichoice Counting Bloom Filter with improved greedy hash allocation and multiple hash groups.
evaluation_criteria: Exposed false negative count, false positive probability, maximum counter load under different hash algorithms.
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: SDBM BUZhash algorithm is less suitable; MCBF needs careful configuration; c cannot be arbitrarily large due to overhead.
evidence_for_taste: we are the first to explore
c should not be too large
